'''Andrew 'Andy' Charles Oates''' (born 1969 in [[Adelaide]], [[Australia]]) is an [[Australians|Australian]] and [[Great Britain|British]] [[Developmental biology|developmental biologist]] and [[Embryology|embryologist]] specialized in biological [[pattern formation]]. He is professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) and head of the Segmentation Timing and Dynamics Laboratory at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]'s School of Life Sciences.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Brexit: closer cooperation with the UK cannot replace participation in Horizon 2020 {{!}} ETH-Board|url=https://www.ethrat.ch/en/medien-medienmitteilungen/brexit-engere-zusammenarbeit-mit-grossbritannien-kann-teilnahme-horizon-2020-nicht-ersetzen|access-date=2020-12-21|website=www.ethrat.ch|archive-date=9 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210109174027/https://www.ethrat.ch/en/medien-medienmitteilungen/brexit-engere-zusammenarbeit-mit-grossbritannien-kann-teilnahme-horizon-2020-nicht-ersetzen}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=oateslab|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/oateslab/|access-date=2020-12-21|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Andrew Charles Oates|url=https://people.epfl.ch/andrew.oates/?lang=en|access-date=2020-12-21|website=people.epfl.ch}}</ref> Since 2021, he has been dean of [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]'s School of Life Sciences.<ref name=":3" />

== Career ==
Oates received an undergraduate degree in [[biochemistry]] with honors for his work at the Robert Saint's laboratory at the [[University of Adelaide]] in 1992. He then joined Andrew F. Wilks at the [[Ludwig Cancer Research|Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research]] and at the [[University of Melbourne]] as PhD student, and graduated in 1998.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nicholson|first1=S. E.|last2=Oates|first2=A. C.|last3=Harpur|first3=A. G.|last4=Ziemiecki|first4=A.|last5=Wilks|first5=A. F.|last6=Layton|first6=J. E.|date=1994-04-12|title=Tyrosine kinase JAK1 is associated with the granulocyte-colony-stimulating factor receptor and both become tyrosine-phosphorylated after receptor activation.|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=91|issue=8|pages=2985–2988|doi=10.1073/pnas.91.8.2985|issn=0027-8424|pmc=43499|pmid=7512720|bibcode=1994PNAS...91.2985N |doi-access=free }}</ref> His postdoctoral time was at the laboratory of Robert Ho both at [[Princeton University]] and at [[University of Chicago]], where he began his studies on the segmentation clock in [[zebrafish]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Oates|first1=Andrew C|last2=Bruce|first2=Ashley E.E|last3=Ho|first3=Robert K|date=August 2000|title=Too Much Interference: Injection of Double-Stranded RNA Has Nonspecific Effects in the Zebrafish Embryo|journal=Developmental Biology|language=en|volume=224|issue=1|pages=20–28|doi=10.1006/dbio.2000.9761|pmid=10898958|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2003, he moved to the [[Max Planck Institute of Molecular Cell Biology and Genetics]] in Dresden to start his research group.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Schröter|first1=Christian|last2=Herrgen|first2=Leah|author3-link=Albert Cardona|last3=Cardona|first3=Albert|last4=Brouhard|first4=Gary J.|last5=Feldman|first5=Benjamin|last6=Oates|first6=Andrew C.|date=March 2008|title=Dynamics of zebrafish somitogenesis|journal=Developmental Dynamics|language=en|volume=237|issue=3|pages=545–553|doi=10.1002/dvdy.21458|pmid=18265021|s2cid=7038940|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Uriu|first1=Koichiro|last2=Ares|first2=Saúl|last3=Oates|first3=Andrew C.|last4=Morelli|first4=Luis G.|date=2013-03-21|title=Dynamics of mobile coupled phase oscillators|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevE.87.032911|journal=Physical Review E|language=en|volume=87|issue=3|article-number=032911|doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.87.032911|bibcode=2013PhRvE..87c2911U |hdl=11336/2452 |issn=1539-3755|hdl-access=free}}</ref> In 2012, he became professor of vertebrate developmental genetics at [[University College London]] and moved his group to the [[National Institute for Medical Research]] at [[Mill Hill]] in [[London]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Soroldoni|first1=D.|last2=Jorg|first2=D. J.|last3=Morelli|first3=L. G.|last4=Richmond|first4=D. L.|last5=Schindelin|first5=J.|last6=Julicher|first6=F.|last7=Oates|first7=A. C.|date=2014-07-11|title=A Doppler effect in embryonic pattern formation|journal=Science|language=en|volume=345|issue=6193|pages=222–225|doi=10.1126/science.1253089|pmid=25013078|s2cid=206556621|issn=0036-8075|pmc=7611034|bibcode=2014Sci...345..222S }}</ref> In April 2015, he became a member of the [[Francis Crick Institute]] in [[London]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=King's College London - Randall Seminar: Professor Andrew Oates|url=https://www.kcl.ac.uk/lsm/newsevents/eventrecords/2015/may/randall-seminar-professor-andrew-oates|access-date=2020-12-21|website=www.kcl.ac.uk}}</ref>

In 2016, he joined [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] as a full professor, where he is the founder and director of the Timing, Oscillation, Patterns Laboratory at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]'s School of Life Sciences.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

Since 2018, he has served as director of the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]'s Institute of Bioengineering,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Sanctuary|first=Hillary|date=2020-08-25|title=Andrew Oates, a Passion for Cycles|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/andrew-oates-a-passion-for-cycles-2/|language=en}}</ref> and since January 2021 he has been the dean of the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]'s School of Life Sciences.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|date=2020-11-12|title=New deans for the Basic Sciences and Life Sciences|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/new-deans-for-the-basic-sciences-and-life-sciences/|language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Oates' research laboratory is composed of [[biologist]]s, [[engineer]]s, and [[physicist]]s. It  draws on [[molecular genetics]], quantitative imaging, and theoretical analysis in order to investigate populations of coupled genetic oscillators in  vertebrate [[embryo]]s, termed as segmentation clocks.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Naganathan|first1=Sundar R.|last2=Oates|first2=Andrew C.|date=October 2017|title=Mechanochemical coupling and developmental pattern formation|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S2452310017300999|journal=Current Opinion in Systems Biology|language=en|volume=5|pages=104–111|doi=10.1016/j.coisb.2017.09.007|url-access=subscription}}</ref> These systems drive the rhythmic, sequential, and precise formation of embryonic body segments, exhibiting rich spatial and temporal phenomena spanning from molecular to tissue scales.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Research|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/oateslab/page-141506-en-html/|access-date=2020-12-21|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lleras Forero|first1=Laura|last2=Narayanan|first2=Rachna|last3=Huitema|first3=Leonie FA|last4=VanBergen|first4=Maaike|last5=Apschner|first5=Alexander|last6=Peterson-Maduro|first6=Josi|last7=Logister|first7=Ive|last8=Valentin|first8=Guillaume|last9=Morelli|first9=Luis G|last10=Oates|first10=Andrew C|last11=Schulte-Merker|first11=Stefan|date=2018-04-06|editor-last=Whitfield|editor-first=Tanya T.|title=Segmentation of the zebrafish axial skeleton relies on notochord sheath cells and not on the segmentation clock|journal=eLife|volume=7|article-number=e33843|doi=10.7554/eLife.33843|pmid=29624170|pmc=5962341|s2cid=4605280|issn=2050-084X|doi-access=free}}</ref>

The laboratory' contributions are the direct connection of genes to segmentation rhythm, and the discovery that the rhythm also involves physical, collective processes at multi-cellular and tissue scales.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Oates|first=Andrew C|date=August 2020|title=Waiting on the Fringe: cell autonomy and signaling delays in segmentation clocks|journal=Current Opinion in Genetics & Development|language=en|volume=63|pages=61–70|doi=10.1016/j.gde.2020.04.008|pmid=32505051|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Venzin|first1=Olivier F.|last2=Oates|first2=Andrew C.|date=April 2020|title=What are you synching about? Emerging complexity of Notch signaling in the segmentation clock|journal=Developmental Biology|language=en|volume=460|issue=1|pages=40–54|doi=10.1016/j.ydbio.2019.06.024|pmid=31302101|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Distinctions ==
Oates is a member of the British Society of Developmental Biology.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Newsletter|url=http://bsdb.org/wp-content/uploads/BSDB-Newsletter-2015-12b.pdf|website=British Society for Developmental Biology}}</ref> He is the recipient of the R.K. Mortenson Prize for Biochemistry 1991.
